The old relation Marcus -> Boreal (on call) isn't in the relation list; we only know facts. I'll consider adding relation: src "Lena", dst "Boreal", rel_kind "on_call_for", evidence "Lena has the Boreal pager this cycle". Hmm, but if the old relation Marcus on_call_for Boreal existed, we'd remove it. We don't know. Safer to just do the correction fact. Actually relations may be useful; but risk of duplicating. I'll keep it minimal: one correction.

Should we also update? The note mentions "Marcus" — existing entity name is "Marcus Oyelaran". The note uses "Marcus" as a different name for existing entity Marcus Oyelaran. Add entity_aliases: name "Marcus", canonical "Marcus Oyelaran", evidence "taking over from Marcus". Yes, that fits: "A name the note uses for an entity that already exists under another name."

Maybe also add a fact that Lena took over from Marcus? That's part of the same info. The correction covers it.

Also should we consider whether the old fact remains (it's time-scoped "to start the year")? Hmm. If the old fact is "to start the year", the new note doesn't necessarily change that statement — it's about a different time period. Adding a new fact "Lena has the Boreal pager as of 2025-02-10" wouldn't contradict. But the memory system treats on-call as current state; the "taking over from Marcus" indicates the transition. I think correction is the right approach — the note says Lena takes over from Marcus, so Marcus is no longer on call. I'll go with the correction.

Alternatively, do both: correction of the old decision + add relation. I'll keep it simple with the correction and the alias.

The task instruction is more specific and later. I'll follow the task instruction: output just the JSON object without code fence.
